title: The Paippalada Samhita of the Atharvaveda
textType: Hymns, charms and speculative verses with prose
dateDisplay: c. 9th–5th century BCE; manuscripts from Kashmir and Orissa
attributionNote: The recension of the Atharvaveda handed down by the Paippalāda school rather than the Śaunaka school, transmitted in a Kashmir manuscript and in a living tradition in Orissa. GRETIL's e-text follows the critical editions of Durgamohan and Dipak Bhattacharya and the kāṇḍa editions of Zehnder, Lubotsky, Griffiths and Kubisch, and was entered by Arlo Griffiths with Thomas Zehnder, Philipp Kubisch, Duccio Lelli, Alexander Lubotsky, Carmen Spiers and Michael Witzel.
description: The Paippalāda Saṃhitā is the second great recension of the Atharvaveda: twenty kāṇḍas of hymns and spells — healing and protection, the winning of a wife or a king's favour, the appeasement of demons and the punishment of enemies, royal consecration, and hymns on the breath, the sun and the cosmic orders — that run parallel to the Śaunaka text, share its core with it and differ from it in wording, order and the presence of verses the received Atharvaveda does not have.
historicalContext: The Paippalāda school is known from the ritual literature of the Atharvaveda and survives as a reciting community in Orissa, whose manuscripts gave the text its second half. The Kashmir manuscript, obtained in 1875, introduced the recension to scholarship, and the twentieth-century editions shown here made it readable alongside the Śaunaka text as the other Atharvaveda.
availabilityNote: Complete as GRETIL publishes it: the whole recension in twenty kāṇḍas, 910 hymns and 7,674 units, streamed from GRETIL one hymn at a time. Each passage is the verse or prose section of one hymn, addressed as kāṇḍa.hymn.verse. This is the original Sanskrit, not a translation.
